findings.evidence: Determinacy.lean:127 `M₁.H ≠ M₂.H`; Determinacy.lean:71 conclusion is `=ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc (-1) 1)]`; Basic.lean:52-55 `Assumptions` constrains only support and `1 < |xi|`, so the single-point model above qualifies.
findings.fix: Strengthen the last conjunct to failure of a.e. equality, e.g. `∃ i xi t, |xi| ≤ 1 ∧ ¬ ((fun x => M₁.H i x xi t) =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc (-1) 1)] fun x => M₂.H i x xi t)` (or: the difference is nonzero on a set of positive measure). It is available from the data already obtained: `p ≠ 0`, so its root set is null and `(Icc 0 1).indicator (p.eval ·)` is not a.e. zero.
findings.issue: `exists_models_mellinMomentH_eq_and_H_ne` concludes `M₁.H ≠ M₂.H`, mere pointwise inequality of functions. The positive result it is advertised to contrast (`ae_eq_of_forall_mellinMomentGpd_eq`, line 67) gives only equality almost everywhere, so pointwise `≠` does not witness any failure of determinacy: the same statement holds for every `N` with ALL moments agreeing, e.g. M₂.H = `if 1 < |xi| then 0 else ({0} : Set ℝ).indicator 1`, which satisfies `Assumptions` and has every moment over `Icc (-1) 1` zero because `{0}` is null. The real content of the construction (p nonzero on a positive-measure set) stays in the proof and never reaches the statement, so the docstring headline "No finite set of Mellin moments determines a GPD" is unsupported by what is proved.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:103 `def InDglapRegion (x xi : ℝ) : Prop := |xi| < |x| ∧ |x| ≤ 1`; Basic.lean:110 `def InErblRegion (x xi : ℝ) : Prop := |x| ≤ |xi|`; Basic.lean:53 `supportH : ∀ i x xi t, x < 0 ∨ 1 < x → M.H i x xi t = 0`.
findings.fix: Drop the DGLAP/ERBL remark here and in the module docstring (lines 31-32), or restate it as "supported in `[0, 1]`, as `GPD.Assumptions` requires of every model".
findings.issue: "the witness is supported in `0 ≤ x ≤ 1`, hence entirely inside the DGLAP region at zero skewness" is false at `x = 0`: `InDglapRegion x 0` unfolds to `|0| < |x| ∧ |x| ≤ 1` (Basic.lean:103), which `x = 0` fails. The companion claim that this shows the ambiguity "is not confined to the central region" is also empty, since `Assumptions.supportH` (Basic.lean:53, `x < 0 ∨ 1 < x → H = 0`) already forces every admissible model into `[0, 1]`, and at `ξ = 0` the ERBL region is `{0}`.

summary: The compact-interval moment determinacy results and the polynomial counterexample are correct, but the headline GPD sharpness theorem concludes only `M₁.H ≠ M₂.H` (pointwise function inequality), which is strictly weaker than the claimed failure of determinacy and is satisfiable with *all* moments equal. One docstring claim about the DGLAP region is also false as written.
